lesson-12.hook: Your order search checks row after row before it finds order forty-two in the table.
lesson-12.recipient: A teammate investigating a slow query
lesson-12.visual: A query cursor scans a table grid. Later follow the same order through an index; illustrate composite-column ordering with the same query.
beats: Apply the actual filter and sort
Show why composite column order matters
Update a row and its index entry
End with query-plan and write-cost checks

lesson-13.hook: Incoming writes are piling up faster than this storage path can drain them.
lesson-13.recipient: An engineer choosing a storage engine
lesson-13.visual: A write backlog grows above a single worker. Trace this write through a tree update versus buffered append, flush and compaction; label alternatives, never imply two mandatory serial engines.
beats: Predict what buffering moves to later
Trace an append and later flush
Compare the read path and amplification

lesson-14.hook: This transfer stops halfway through the update when the database suddenly crashes.
lesson-14.visual: One transfer reaches a crash boundary. Carry the same transfer through two row changes, a local transaction and WAL recovery; distinguish uncommitted work from durable commit.
beats: Expose the partial-update risk without a transaction
Show the log before acknowledging durable commit
Recover or roll back the same transaction
lesson-14.ending: One controlled-crash test and one external-side-effect check

lesson-15.hook: The product page returns yesterday’s price even though the source already changed.
lesson-15.recipient: A teammate building a read model
lesson-15.visual: Read a stale product price from a read-optimized copy. Keep the product ID visible as the source changes, copy catches up, and a reader observes the update.
beats: Show a stale result from the copy
Show the propagation gap and repair
End with freshness and reconciliation checks
lesson-15.ending: One freshness rule and one reconciliation check

lesson-16.hook: The video reaches object storage before its final record exists in the database.
lesson-16.visual: A file token reaches object storage directly. Keep metadata and bytes distinct; show scoped upload permission, validation, finalization and an orphan when finalization fails.
beats: Show bytes arriving without final metadata
Ask what a completed upload means
Send bytes directly to object storage

lesson-17.hook: This identifier finds a record, but its timestamp cannot prove what happened first.
lesson-17.visual: An ID token finds a record, then show independently generated IDs and physical index placement. Contrast random and time-ordered choices without promising causal order or zero collisions.
beats: Show an ID locating the record
Generate IDs independently on two servers
Separate time order from causal order
